subject: Changing behavior of obj function values

messages.author: 1ad83de047b5ec8d
messages.subject: Changing behavior of obj function values
parts:
Hi,

I'm starting to explore TMB and came across the following:

1. Create an obj with MakeADFun()
2. Check values of obj$fn(), obj$gr(), etc
3. After optimization, this values change, since, as I understand, the value of obj$env$last.par gets updated, and those functions are evaluated at last.par

So far as I can understand, this happens because obj$env is an environment and can be dynamically changed. Ok, but as I was exploring, sometimes I use numDeriv functions, such as grad() and hessian() to understand some calculations. So, when I use, e.g.,

numDeriv::grad(obj$fn, obj$par)

to compare with obj$gr(), the value in obj$env$last.par changes and that affect all other things we can do with obj functions.

As an example, please see the following (rendered) script at: http://leg.ufpr.br/~fernandomayer/misc/tmbexample.html. This is a very simple example where this behavior happens, and the differences there are very small, but I've seen other examples where the difference in obj$env$last.par (compared to opt$par, for example) after calling some numDeriv function was significantly different.

So, I understand that obj$env$last.par is dynamically modified, but can numDeriv (or other packages) functions also modify it? If so, what is the recommendation to avoid this pattern?

Also, how can I know how exactly this "dynamical" change in obj$env$last.par happens? I tried to find something in the documentation but was not successful. 

Thanks in advance,

---
Fernando de Pol Mayer
Laboratório de Estatística e Geoinformação - LEG
Departamento de Estatística - DEST
Universidade Federal do Paraná - UFPR
URL: http://leg.ufpr.br/~fernandomayer

messages.author: 395bdca538bcae5d
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Changing behavior of obj function values
parts:
Hi Fernando,

Presumably Numderiv::grad just calls the obj$fn with perturbations for finite differences and you're seeing the last one that it called. That seems to make sense to me. If you're doing that a lot and then using obj for other things, like report(), then I can see how you'd have issues. Perhaps the safest thing is to always pass the MLE values when calling those so it is explicit and safe which values are used.

More generally, the obj$env$last.par approach is rather unusual even for experienced R users, in my opinion. Kasper do you mind commenting on why you chose this approach and ways in which users *should not* use it? I.e., what are some pitfalls that may not be obvious to users?

Cheers,
Cole

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Changing behavior of obj function values
parts:
I've added a note to the documentation (?MakeADFun) that one should not rely upon the default arguments of any of the model object functions.
Always use explicit function arguments:

numDeriv::grad(obj$fn, obj$par)
obj$gr(obj$par)

The last.par default was mainly intended for the following construct:

obj$fn(opt$par)  ## Get likelihood and update internal 'last.par'
obj$gr()         ## Gradient for opt$par
obj$he()         ## Hessian for opt$par
obj$report()     ## Report for opt$par

Given the confusion it generates I admit the last.par default might have been a bad decision. However, it's not going to change...

And you're right - it's safer to always use explicit arguments. I believe the note in the documentation will clarify this and prevent other users from the same issue.

Thanks again,
